subtype: Approach: trying several hobbies and never settling [Pitfall]
passage: At the community centre notice board, Irfan signed up for football on Mondays, guitar on Wednesdays and coding on Fridays, all in the first week of the month. By week three his calendar was full and his fingertips hurt, his football boots were always in the wrong bag, and the coding puzzle still showed the same error. Coach Harish watched him miss an easy pass. "Your mind is somewhere else, Irfan." "Everywhere else," Irfan muttered. On Friday he stared at the blank screen, felt his shoulders sag and thought maybe he was just no good at anything. He shut the laptop and left before the class ended.

qa.q: Which three activities did Irfan sign up for?
qa.a: Irfan signed up for football, guitar and coding.

qa.q: What did Irfan feel on Friday while staring at the blank screen?
qa.a: Discouraged, since his shoulders sagged and he thought he might be no good at anything.

qa.q: What could Irfan try instead of three activities at once?
qa.a: Pick one activity for a month and return to the others later, because focused time brings visible progress.

qa.q: How might Coach Harish see the missed pass?
qa.a: As a sign that Irfan is stretched too thin, since Harish said Irfan's mind was somewhere else.

grounding: A child begins football, guitar and coding in a single month and, with too little time for each, makes little progress and loses heart.

subtype: Approach: trying several hobbies and never settling [Pitfall]
passage: Ira lives across the landing, so I saw most of it. In the first week of June she came home with football boots. The next week it was a second-hand guitar, and by the third week Parveen Aunty had signed her up for a coding class on Saturdays. Monday football, Wednesday guitar, Saturday coding. I heard the guitar through the wall for maybe ten minutes on Thursdays, the same three chords. At the end of the month she sat on the stairs with her boots untied. "I can't do any of them," she told me. "My passing is bad, my fingers hurt and my code never runs." I don't know if she was more tired or more sad. Parveen Aunty came out and sat beside her for a long time.

qa.q: Which day was Ira's coding class?
What did Ira seem to feel sitting on the stairs?
qa.a: She seemed discouraged and tired, sure she could not do any of the three, though the narrator couldn't tell which feeling was stronger.

qa.q: What would you suggest Ira change first?
qa.a: Pick one hobby to focus on for a couple of months, so there is time to get past the hard early stage and actually improve.

qa.q: How might Parveen Aunty see the month?
qa.a: She may feel concerned and partly responsible for signing Ira up, and sitting beside her suggests she wants to help her choose what to keep.

grounding: An observer watches a child start football, guitar and coding in one month, progress little in each and lose heart.

subtype: Approach: trying several hobbies and never settling [Pitfall]
passage:
1 September. Baljeet has a plan for the month: football on Mondays, keyboard lessons on Wednesdays, a coding club on Fridays. Ojas, his best friend, says it sounds like a lot. Baljeet says it sounds like everything.
15 September. He forgot his keyboard exercise because of football. At coding club he spends the whole hour catching up on last week's task. He plays the same two lines on the keyboard over and over and can't get the third.
30 September. At the end-of-month football match Baljeet sits on the bench. His keyboard teacher writes "Practise more" in his book. His code still won't draw a square. He tells Ojas, "I'm bad at everything," and kicks a pebble all the way home.

qa.q: Which day was the coding club?
qa.a: The coding club was on Fridays.

qa.q: What was Baljeet feeling when he told Ojas he was bad at everything?
qa.a: He felt discouraged and frustrated, because after a month of three hobbies he had little to show in any of them.

qa.q: What could Baljeet try in October instead?
qa.a: Choose one of the three and give it the extra evenings, so he has enough time to practise between lessons and see real progress.

qa.q: How might Ojas see Baljeet's month?
qa.a: Ojas doubted the plan from the start, so he may feel sorry for Baljeet rather than surprised, and want to cheer him up.

grounding: Shows over a month how starting football, keyboard and coding together leaves a child with little progress and feeling discouraged.
